chunks: What was narrated to us by the Sheikh — may Allah the Exalted support him — from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, who said:
Abu Maryam al-Ansari mentioned that al-Hakam ibn 'Utaybah urinated one day and did not wash his penis intentionally. So I mentioned that to Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him).
He (the Imam) said: 'How evil is what he did! He must wash his penis and repeat his salat, but he does not need to repeat his wudu.'

key_terms.بِئْسَ: how evil, how wretched (Arabic verb of dispraise, dhamma)

ai.seo_question: According to Imam al-Sadiq (AS), does intentionally neglecting to wash the penis after urination invalidate one's wudu, or does it only require repeating the salat?
ai.summary: Ibn Udhaynah reports that Abu Maryam al-Ansari informed him that al-Hakam ibn 'Utaybah — a Kufi Sunni jurist — intentionally urinated without washing his penis. When Ibn Udhaynah relayed this to Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the Imam condemned the act and issued a precise ruling: the person must wash his penis and repeat his salat, but his wudu remains valid and need not be repeated. This ruling distinguishes between the invalidation of the prayer (due to najasah on the body) and the continuing validity of the wudu (which was performed before the najasah was incurred).
